unit: author re-verification of the independent v3 review
engine: PostgreSQL 17.11, disposable local cluster, destroyed after use

F1_completeFunctionClaimOnlyTrueForLedge.evidence: gab3-admission-function.sql contains no hmac, no vault, no decrypted_secret, no INSERT into flags or feedback. limiter.admit() takes p_bucket bytea already formed. The MECHANISM section claims one function does the HMAC, the ledger decision and the INSERT - that combined function does not exist as tested code.
F1_completeFunctionClaimOnlyTrueForLedge.significance: Same defect class as v2 Finding 5, relocated to the derivation and enforcement half of the pipeline. v3's changelog claim is accurate only for the concurrency step v2 Finding 5 named.

F2_bucketPurgeBreaksTheCeiling.verdict: FALSIFIED THE INVARIANT - REPRODUCED BY AUTHOR
F2_bucketPurgeBreaksTheCeiling.method: Mint a grant on one bucket, spend 3, delete ONLY the bucket row (simulating a per-table retention job), replay the surviving grant.
observed: before purge: bucket units=3, grant units=3
after bucket-only purge, replay same grant -> ADMITTED remaining=6
bucket row silently recreated at 0 then incremented to 1
grant units=4 (true cumulative) while the bucket records 1
F2_bucketPurgeBreaksTheCeiling.significance: The bucket's recorded consumption UNDERSTATES true consumption after a purge, so total consumption can exceed BUCKET_ALLOWANCE. This is the exact invariant the starvation fix rests on, and it fails in the unsafe direction (more consumption, not less).

fixVerifiedByAuthor.change: FOREIGN KEY limiter.grant (bucket_key, window_id) REFERENCES limiter.bucket ON DELETE CASCADE
fixVerifiedByAuthor.observed: after the same bucket purge, surviving grant rows = 0 (cascaded away, no orphan); replaying the old grant issues a fresh grant and the ceiling holds

F2_bucketPurgeBreaksTheCeiling.note: No purge SQL or scheduled job exists anywhere in the evidence - the retention step is prose only, and pg_cron availability for this project remains UNVERIFIED (carried from v1 Finding 15 / v2 Finding 12).

F3_privacyRegression.verdict: CONFIRMED - and the author flagged this to the reviewer as a suspected self-introduced regression before the review ran
F3_privacyRegression.detail: window_id is mixed into the HMAC MESSAGE, not the key, so one long-lived secret spans every window. An actor with ledger access in this project plausibly also holds the elevated role needed to read vault.decrypted_secrets, and can forward-compute the bucket key for ANY window the secret has covered - a strictly stronger capability than v2's destroyed-per-window secret gave the same actor. No rotation interval, deletion step or precedent is specified.
F3_privacyRegression.significance: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS 6 and 7 currently understate exposure as roughly one live window. The true bound is however long any historical secret value plus any backup or PITR snapshot survives, which is presently unbounded.

F6_twoKnobsNotOne.significance: BUCKET_ALLOWANCE is the only refusal CEILING, but NORMAL remains an independent fairness knob. v3's 'single policy number' wording is an overstatement.

F7_pgcryptoSearchPathLandmine.verdict: ACCEPTED AS A REAL RISK, UNVERIFIED against hosted Supabase by the author
F7_pgcryptoSearchPathLandmine.detail: limiter.admit sets search_path to 'limiter','pg_temp'. Supabase installs pgcrypto into the extensions schema, so an unqualified hmac() call in the still-unwritten wrapper would fail at runtime. Must be schema-qualified and explicitly tested.

F5_droppedV2Findings.detail: v3 has NO rollback section at all (v2 Finding 11 lever-independence concern unaddressed), and does not differentiate network-rotation difficulty by connection type (v2 Finding 9). Neither is claimed as fixed, but both are dropped from the record while v3 declares it supersedes v2.

reviewerConfirmations: All eight v3 local tests reproduced exactly from the verbatim artifact.

New adversarial cases passed: 50-way same-grant reuse (no double-spend), 100-way across 10 buckets (no deadlock), negative/zero/INT_MAX parameters fail safe, empty/duplicate limiter.config fails toward enabled.

The Cloudflare trust boundary reproduced live with clean negative controls: only cf-connecting-ip triggers the 403/error-1000 block, including on OPTIONS preflight; x-real-ip, true-client-ip and x-forwarded-for pass through normally.
Bypass mechanics re-verified against the real schema, including that feedback_insert_self_or_anon has no TO clause.
netAssessment: V3_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW: HOLD. The ledger core is sound and independently reproduced. Three MUST-FIX items stand, one of which (F2) falsifies the invariant underpinning v3's headline starvation fix. A verified fix exists for F2 but is not yet incorporated or re-reviewed.
